building_name: The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints Institute of Religion
reviewer: independent evaluator r2; raw official GIS, first-party location sources, Street View photograph, three renders, and Blender 5.2.3 direct reopen

criteria.status: official GIS identity/address and the assigned wall ring verified
evidence: Raw Purdue GIS FID 779 names Lds Institute of Religion at 14 WALDRON ST.; the first-party Church location index lists the West Lafayette Waldron and Jasper Street locations separately.

The current Blender mesh's four lower shell corners match the transformed official GIS ring within 0.000016 m maximum nearest-corner distance. The separate access ramp lies outside the wall ring and is treated as ancillary geometry.

The preserved July 2023 Street View image shows the long, low brick Institute building across the street at the mapped Waldron location; the separate Jasper Street meetinghouse is not used as a source.

criteria.status: GIS campus placement and plan scale reproduced
evidence: Direct Blender 5.2.3 reopen confirms XY mesh bounds X -342.526..-319.107 m and Y -306.716..-273.774 m; transformed GIS wall ring is approximately 18.77 m east-west by 32.94 m north-south.

The footprint orientation follows the official north-south major axis and retains the library's direct campus-world coordinates. The GIS ring conversion uses the repository's documented local approximation.

criteria.criterion: Evidence-backed height, floors, and roof form
criteria.status: one-story low building and secondary roof glimpse are supported; heights and roof plan are estimates
evidence: Purdue GIS records NUM_LEVELS=1; the July 2023 view shows a one-story low roof and a reddish raised roof section behind the main dark roof.
Reopened mesh bounds reach 5.90 m and the builder estimates 4.15 m eaves, 5.45 m main ridge, and 5.90 m secondary ridge. These vertical values are not measured by an elevation/survey source.

GIS field `Extrution` is 12 but its units are undocumented, so it cannot independently validate modeled metric height. The one available photo is oblique and tree-occluded; it does not establish roof pitch, hidden roof footprint, or wall heights.
findings: Keep the vertical datums and secondary roof plan explicitly estimated; no scaled section/elevation or measured height source was found.

criteria.status: material palette and entrance/ramp concept are photo-supported; composition is only approximate
evidence: The direct July 2023 image supports a red-brown brick exterior, dark low main roof, reddish higher roof behind, a broad glazed/recessed entrance zone, brick piers, ramp/steps, and small windows.

The current west-facade render includes those general elements, including recessed glazing and an access ramp. Its entry zone sits farther toward the middle of the long wall than the source image's strongly off-center entrance; the source's glazed front zone/brick-pier arrangement is not closely reproduced.

The model has two small, widely separated windows and a broad simple entry screen. Window count, exact position, framing, roof material and stationing remain estimates from one oblique view; the tree-obscured and unseen facades have no direct visual support.
findings: Refine the entry stationing and the recessed multi-bay glazing/brick-pier composition against the photograph; retain a clear uncertainty note for the unobserved facades and roof section.
